newsitem.title: FRANCE: Licoys will help Havas offensive - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Licoys will help Havas offensive - chairman.

text.p: The appointment of Eric Licoys as managing director of Havas, announced on Tuesday, will help it to carry out its aggressive strategy, Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier said in a newspaper interview published on Wednesday.
"We could, for example, envisage initiatives notably in publishing, in the context of a strategy of international growth," Dauzier told financial daily La Tribune.
"My objective is, with Eric Licoys, to implement our strategy in the new markets opened up by the convergence of communication and telecommunications," Dauzier said.
"The objective is to offer consumers a range of fee-based services in these new medias," he said.

Dauzier reiterated that he wanted to find the same kind of international alliance for units Havas Advertising and CEP Communication as had been found for pay TV firm Canal Plus, in which Havas holds 34.4 percent, through Canal Plus's recent merger with Nethold.

He also reiterated that Havas was examining its relations with Bertelsmann's CLT-UFA, and that its stake in its travel agency unit, Havas Voyages, could change to release funds for the unit's development.

Dauzier told an analysts meeting in April that Havas would either increase its 10 percent stake in CLT or sell out altogether, but this could only happen after a contract between Havas's IP and CLT's radio stations reached its term in the year 2000.
He also said then that Havas was constrained in opening the capital of Havas Voyages to another shareholder by an accord with American Express on business travel which has another two years to run.

Licoys, who is currently the adviser to Jean-Marie Messier, the chairman of Havas's main shareholder, Cie Generale des Eaux, was previously chairman of Lazard Freres' Fonds-Partenaires-Gestion and before that was managing director of Barclay's French investment bank.
He is due to take up his post at Havas on June 26.
